
══════════════════════════════════════════
  HUNT: Process Injection
══════════════════════════════════════════

  VERDICT     HIGH CONFIDENCE INJECTION
  Confidence  high
  Score       3/3
  Coverage    PARTIAL
  Review      high

  KEY SIGNALS

  Live execution in a correlated allocation  [HIGH]  DETECTION  (injection.allocation_correlation)
    Inference   : 1 thread(s) currently execute inside an allocation that is simultaneously RWX and
                  hosts a validated hidden PE — page type, structural PE validation, and live
                  RIP/EIP all converge on the same AllocationBase.
    Confidence  : high — This is the strongest evidence this hunter can produce: the process is, at
                  the moment of the dump, actively running code from an allocation with no
                  legitimate module backing and a concealed PE image.
    Facts:
      - TID=0x1 RIP=0x7ff700002000 -> VA=0x7ff700002000 AllocationBase=0x7ff700000000 size=0x1000
        type=MEM_PRIVATE protect=PAGE_READWRITE [FULL: RWX+validated-PE]
    Limitations:
      - RIP is a single-point-in-time snapshot; a thread that executed there moments before or after
        the dump was captured would not appear here.

  RWX memory  [MEDIUM]  LEAD  (injection.rwx_regions)
    Inference   : 1 memory region(s) carry PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE/WRITECOPY protection, spanning 1
                  distinct allocation(s).
    Confidence  : medium — RWX is a directly-observed page protection flag, not a heuristic guess —
                  but RWX alone is routinely used by JITs, debuggers, and some legitimate packers,
                  so it is a lead, not proof, until corroborated by a validated PE header and/or
                  live execution in the same allocation.
    Facts:
      - VA (process)=0x00007ff700000000 size=0x1000 AllocationBase=0x00007ff700000000
        File_offset=(not captured) PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE MEM_PRIVATE
    Limitations:
      - Does not by itself distinguish injection from JIT/legitimate self-modifying-code use cases.

  Hidden PE header  [MEDIUM]  LEAD  (injection.hidden_pe_validated)
    Inference   : 1 region(s) contain a structurally-valid PE header (DOS+COFF+optional header+full
                  section table all parsed successfully) at an address absent from the module list,
                  in MEM_PRIVATE memory, an executable unbacked mapping, or otherwise correlated
                  with an RWX allocation or live thread execution.
    Confidence  : medium — Passing full structural PE validation (not just an 'MZ' prefix) rules out
                  coincidental bytes and most decoys, but a valid header outside the module list can
                  also occur from a manually-mapped but otherwise benign in-process library (e.g.
                  some anti-cheat/DRM loaders) — confidence rises to HIGH only when a thread's live
                  RIP/EIP actually executes inside the same allocation.
    Facts:
      - VA (process)=0x00007ff700002000 AllocationBase=0x00007ff700000000 File_offset=(not captured)
        Page_type=MEM_PRIVATE PAGE_READWRITE PE_machine=AMD64 PE_sections=1 Entry_point_RVA=0x1000
        Declared_ImageBase=0x140000000
    Limitations:
      - Header validation read is capped at 4096 bytes; a section table extending past that reports
        as invalid rather than being partially trusted.

  Unbacked thread start  [LOW]  LEAD  (injection.unbacked_thread_startaddress)
    Inference   : 1 thread(s) began execution at an address not covered by any known module.
    Confidence  : low — StartAddress records where a thread BEGAN, not where it is executing now — a
                  thread can legitimately start inside unbacked/JIT memory (e.g. a thread pool
                  worker routine passed as a raw function pointer into private memory) and still be
                  benign. Current RIP/EIP (below, when available) is the stronger signal for what a
                  thread is actually doing.
    Facts:
      - TID=0x1 StartAddress_VA=0x00007ff700002000 File_offset=(not captured)

  COVERAGE

  [~] PARTIAL
      1 region(s) returned fewer bytes than requested while checking for hidden PE headers (short
      read) — not fully examined
